articles.summary: By Ray DeMoss, Support Manager If you work in high-performance compute (HPC) or system support, running lspci -vvv is almost muscle memory. It is your first window into the PCIe bus: checking negotiated speed, link width, and device status. When a system in an air-conditioned laboratory drops bandwidth, lspci usually tells you enough to start troubleshooting. But when compute platforms move out of the data center and into harsh edge environments—like inside autonomous ground vehicles, mobile command centers, or aircraft—lspci quickly hits its limits. At PCIe Gen5 (32 GT/s) and Gen6 (64 GT/s), electrical tolerances shrink to nanosecond margins. When a high-density GPU or NVMe storage array suddenly negotiates down to Gen1 speeds or drops from a x16 to a x4 link width, lspci confirms that the failure happened, but it cannot tell you why. Was it a thermal drift changing trace impedance? Connector fretting from chassis vibration? Or did the system simply step down to conserve power? To keep high-throughput edge AI systems operational without bringing expensive oscilloscopes into the field, support and test engineers need to move past standard status commands and utilize in-band hardware telemetry. In this article, we demonstrate how to leverage native Linux utilities like pcicrawler, kernel Advanced Error Reporting (AER) logs, and software-driven Receiver Eye Margining (pcilmr) to diagnose physical layer signal degradation, isolate link down-training, and maintain peak PCIe Gen4/Gen5/Gen6 fabric performance at the edge. Down-Training vs. ASPM: Distinguishing Faults from Power Saving One of the most common false alarms in field diagnostics occurs when a high-speed PCIe endpoint reports running at 2.5 GT/s (PCIe Gen1). Before disassembling a rugged chassis or replacing cables, you must determine whether the link is physically degraded or simply idling. Active State Power Management (ASPM) intentionally drops PCIe link speeds during idle periods to reduce power consumption and thermal load. However, under physical stress, the PCIe Link Training and Status State Machine (LTSSM) may encounter bit errors and permanently down-train the link to maintain a stable connection. To isolate the root cause in the field, force the kernel's ASPM policy to performance mode: echo performance > /sys/module/pcie_aspm/parameters/policy If putting the system under load restores the link to maximum rate, ASPM was active. If the device remains locked at degraded speeds or narrower widths, you are dealing with physical layer signal degradation. Automated Bus Inspection Beyond Standard Command Outputs Parsing massive PCI bus trees manually during field testing is inefficient. Open-source utilities like pcicrawler allow engineers to dump the complete PCIe topology into structured JSON. By filtering current link performance against maximum capable device specs, down-trained endpoints can be flagged immediately: pcicrawler -j | jq -r '.[] | select(.cur_speed != .capable_speed or .cur_width != .capable_width) |
articles.title: Beyond lspci: How to Debug & Maintain High-Density PCIe Gen5/Gen6 Fabrics at the Edge

articles.summary: Final round of PGE Corporation Foundation grants completes a five-year, $2.5 million investment in 25 community organizations Link to the B-roll and soundbite from Sacramento Splash The PGE Corporation Foundation (PGE Foundation) is awarding five community-based organizations in Northern and Central California a total of $500,000 in grants for local initiatives dedicated to environmental stewardship. The 2026 grant recipients represent the program's final group, completing the PGE Foundation's five-year investment in projects that help strengthen local ecosystems and communities. Since its launch in 2022, the Better Together Nature Positive Innovation Grant Program has invested $2.5 million in 25 organizations across Pacific Gas and Electric Company's (PGE) service area, advancing environmental stewardship and supporting community-led innovation. The five organizations will each receive $100,000 through the Better Together Nature Positive Innovation Grant
